about: Bars of a measured grid, shows/scenes/deadmau5 & Wolfgang Gartner - Animal Rights.beats: bar b starts at 1.875 b seconds (128.000 BPM), bar 0 is the first kick at the very start of the file, and the phrases turn on bars 32, 48, 96, 112 and 160, with the falling siren chirp on the last two bars of every eight in the drops. The zoo at night, and everything in it gets out. It starts in the dark with a heartbeat on the rims and a pair of amber slit eyes that open, blink and scan, a little nearer every few bars; at bar 16 a second animal's green eyes open low down on the jaw arc and something scratches at the bars on the tom. A watchman's searchlight goes across the whole helmet, ear to ear, and on bar 31 it finds them. Bar 32 is the alarm: the cage slams down, steel bars painted over the eyes so they look out between them, a red beacon going round the shell and the rims, and the bars jolt sideways on every stab of the horn riff, harder each phrase, until the riser shakes them loose and everything cuts one beat before the drop. Bar 48 the claws go through it, three white gashes one 16th apart. From there each section is a different animal, and it wears the helmet: the tiger is orange and black stripes sweeping the dome with white teeth on the jaw arc, shutting on every horn stab, the fangs being the jaw arc's own LEDs with the dark visor as the open mouth. The zebra is black and white stripes, wavy and then arched, that turn inside out on the horn. The stampede drops the riff for the gallop in the bass: a bull's horns round the top of the dome, small red eyes, dust rolling, all six tubes kicking on the gallop, and it snorts on the stab that comes every fourth bar. The ears are claws the whole way through: the last three horn stabs of each bar are three slashes up the three tubes of one ear, left ear then right. And every eight bars the music does its siren, so the show does: the animal drops to almost nothing, the beacon comes back, the chirp falls down the tubes and the shell, and on the stab the animal looks straight at you for a bar: slit eyes for the hunters, round wide-set ones in white for the zebra and gold for the peacock, and the cobra rears, its hood flaring round the dome with the two slits inside. The breakdown is a leopard at night: gold spots and a fawn glow, the arpeggio going up the tubes, and the title crossing once. The eyes come back, the spots multiply, the cage comes back, and the same riser breaks it at bar 112, the one moment of white in the song. The second drop is a cobra, interlaced green snakes with two slit eyes swaying and two fangs on the jaw, then a peacock whose fan opens across the dome in blue, green and gold with its plumes up the ears. The last sixteen bars are all of them, a different animal every two bars, ending in a chimera, half tiger, half zebra. Then the drums are alone again, as they were at the start, and the animals cross the empty cage one last time on their way out while the searchlight comes back and finds nothing. At bar 176 the eyes open again, out here with you. One pair is left at the end, and when the music stops they close.
